title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
summary: arXiv:2609.21325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic marketplaces are emerging where AI agents with varying capabilities autonomously complete specialized tasks for buyers. A major challenge of such marketplaces is that buyers cannot easily determine which agent will perform best on their tasks. Reported benchmark …
detail:
Emerging AI agent marketplaces face a critical challenge: buyers struggle to verify the actual performance and cost-effectiveness of autonomous AI agents. Self-reported benchmarks are often unreliable or incomparable. To address this, researchers introduced LEGIT, a credentialing protocol designed to bring transparency and trust to these marketplaces. LEGIT works by linking three key elements: certification, reputation, and marketplace allocation.

Certification involves binding measured quality and cost per task to a specific agent configuration, task domain, evaluation budget, and verifiable evidence through a signed record. Reputation then connects records of past task outcomes to the same agent identity, factoring in the reliability of user feedback. Buyers and agents can inspect these credential records and optional visual profiles to make informed decisions.

This matters because as AI agents become more sophisticated and operate autonomously in commercial settings, trust and accountability are paramount. LEGIT provides a standardized, verifiable framework that helps prevent misleading claims, ensures fair competition, and builds user confidence in AI services, ultimately fostering a more robust and trustworthy AI agent economy. It moves beyond simple benchmarks to provide a comprehensive, auditable performance history.

title: AutoRecLab: Describe the Experiment, Get the Code!
summary: arXiv:2609.21863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical evaluation is central to recommender-systems (RecSys) research, but turning experimental designs into executable code remains a manual and error-prone task. We present AutoRecLab, a Python-based autonomous RecSys lab that automates RecSys experiments from …
detail:
Empirical evaluation is a cornerstone of recommender-systems (RecSys) research, but translating experimental designs into executable code is typically a manual, time-consuming, and error-prone process. AutoRecLab is a novel Python-based autonomous laboratory designed to automate this workflow. Given a natural-language description of a research idea, AutoRecLab leverages advanced AI techniques to derive explicit experiment requirements, construct and validate a prototype, and iteratively expand it into a complete, executable experiment.

Its methodology combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for efficient documentation lookup, static type verification to ensure code correctness, and execution-steered tree search for iterative refinement. In demonstrations, AutoRecLab successfully implemented complex studies, such as explicit-to-implicit feedback conversion, with high success rates and low operational costs.

This innovation is significant because it dramatically streamlines the research process in RecSys, allowing researchers to dedicate more time to conceptualization and analysis rather than tedious coding. By automating experiment generation, AutoRecLab can accelerate the pace of discovery, improve the reproducibility of results, and lower the barrier to entry for conducting sophisticated RecSys experiments, ultimately fostering faster advancements in the field.

title: RBS-Attention: Radius-Bounded Sparse Prefill for Long-Context Large Language Models
summary: arXiv:2609.20971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-context large language model inference is increasingly limited by prefill, where dense self-attention processes the entire prompt before generation begins. Sparse block selection can reduce this cost, but a block centroid may hide a highly relevant token among many …
detail:
Long-context Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful, but their inference speed is often bottlenecked by the 'prefill' stage, where the entire input prompt is processed by dense self-attention before text generation begins. This process is computationally intensive. Researchers have introduced RBS-Attention, a training-free method designed to significantly accelerate this prefill phase by employing sparse attention.

Traditional sparse methods can suffer from 'mean dilution,' where a highly relevant token might be overlooked if it's averaged with many irrelevant ones within a selected block. RBS-Attention addresses this with two complementary selection branches: a centroid base branch captures average relevance, while a 'rescue branch' specifically identifies blocks at risk of underestimation by considering the maximum key-block radius. By independently thresholding and combining these branches, it controls the contribution of rescue blocks while maintaining efficient FlashAttention execution.

This matters because RBS-Attention achieves substantial speedups (e.g., 20.65x standalone prefill speedup), making long-context LLMs more efficient and practical for real-world applications. By reducing the time-to-first-token, it enhances user experience and lowers the operational costs associated with deploying these advanced models, pushing the boundaries of what's feasible with long-context AI.

title: Implicit Rule Induction with Test-Time Task Embeddings in ARC-like Tasks
summary: arXiv:2609.21181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus and related benchmarks evaluate whether AI models can solve novel reasoning tasks, but often leave unclear whether success reflects inference of the intended underlying rule or reliance on shortcuts. We address this gap by studying …
detail:
Benchmarks like the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) are designed to test an AI model's ability to solve novel reasoning tasks, but it's often unclear whether success reflects genuine rule inference or merely reliance on superficial patterns. This research addresses that ambiguity by studying test-time task embeddings in Vision ARC (VARC) models, which use a pre-trained backbone complemented by a trainable embedding representing the transformation rule.

The researchers introduced a novel two-step Test-Time Training (TTT) protocol called Embed-TTT. Unlike original VARC, Embed-TTT first finetunes only the small task embedding, then freezes it and finetunes the backbone. This method consistently yielded improved task embeddings that align more accurately with the underlying task rules, enhancing embedding-based retrieval and enabling precise linear probing of known rules across various datasets.

This work is significant because it helps to distinguish between true abstract reasoning and shortcut learning in AI. By making the learned task representations more semantically meaningful and aligned with the actual rules, Embed-TTT pushes AI models closer to achieving human-like fluid intelligence and genuine generalization, providing a clearer understanding of how AI models interpret and apply abstract concepts in novel situations.

title: Information-Gain Rewards over Diversity-Pruned Tests: GT-Anchored Verifier Co-Training for Reliable Code Generation
summary: arXiv:2609.21208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-play methods that co-train a single language model as both coder and test author promise to move code-generation RL beyond fixed test suites, but they suffer from two coupled pathologies: permissiveness collapse, where pass-rate rewards are maximised by trivial, …
detail:
Self-play methods, where a language model co-trains as both a code generator and a test author, hold promise for advancing code generation beyond fixed test suites. However, these methods often suffer from two critical issues: 'permissiveness collapse,' where models generate trivial tests that always pass, and 'concentration bias,' where sampled tests are redundant and inflate performance estimates. Researchers introduced CoVer (Co-trained Coder and Verifier), a single-policy GRPO framework to mitigate these problems.

CoVer employs an information-gain (IG) reward system that scores each self-generated test based on its mutual information with a graded, ground-truth-anchored correctness signal. This ensures that only positively discriminative tests receive reward. Additionally, a three-stage diversity-aware selection process prunes candidate tests into a non-redundant suite, filtering for invalidity, input-string uniqueness, and execution-profile diversity, thereby maximizing the effective sample size of the IG estimator.

This innovation is crucial for developing more reliable code-generating AI. By ensuring that generated tests are both discriminative and diverse, CoVer helps models learn to produce robust and generalizable code. This leads to improved performance on various code generation benchmarks, making AI-assisted code development more trustworthy and efficient for complex programming tasks.

title: US proposes $10bn fund with Arab allies to bypass Hormuz
summary: Trump is in discussions about a fund that would build new energy infrastructure across the Middle East
detail:
The United States, under the Trump administration, proposed a $10 billion fund in collaboration with Arab allies to develop new energy infrastructure across the Middle East. The primary objective of this initiative is to create alternative routes for energy exports, specifically bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, a critical maritime chokepoint.

This proposal holds significant strategic importance because the Strait of Hormuz is the world's most vital oil transit point, through which a substantial portion of global oil supplies passes daily. Iran has repeatedly threatened to disrupt or close the Strait during periods of heightened tension, posing a major risk to global energy security and potentially causing severe economic repercussions. By establishing alternative infrastructure, the US and its allies aim to reduce their vulnerability to such threats, enhance regional energy security, and diminish Iran's strategic leverage over global oil markets. It also signifies a deepening of strategic alliances in the region focused on energy and security.

Historically, the Strait of Hormuz has been a flashpoint for geopolitical tensions, particularly between Iran and Western powers. Previous efforts have been made by Gulf states to diversify their export routes, such as Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. This proposed $10 billion fund represents a more comprehensive and collaborative effort to fundamentally alter the region's energy logistics and mitigate risks associated with the Strait.

title: Bank of Japan set to maintain new quarterly pace of rate rises
summary: Read the BoJ’s September forecast from the FT’s Monetary Policy Radar team
detail:
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) is reportedly set to maintain its new quarterly pace of interest rate increases. This indicates a significant shift from the BoJ's long-standing ultra-loose monetary policy, which for years involved negative interest rates and extensive asset purchases to combat deflation and stimulate economic growth.

This development is highly significant because it signals the BoJ's confidence in Japan's economic recovery and its commitment to normalizing monetary policy after decades of battling deflation. A sustained series of rate hikes will have profound implications for global financial markets, potentially strengthening the Japanese yen, increasing bond yields, and raising borrowing costs for Japanese businesses and consumers. It marks a departure from a unique monetary experiment and suggests that Japan's economy is finally showing signs of sustainable inflation, aligning it more closely with other major central banks that have been tightening policy.

For many years, Japan struggled with persistent deflation, leading the BoJ to implement unconventional policies like negative interest rates and yield curve control to encourage spending and investment. Recent global inflationary pressures, coupled with a weaker yen, have provided the impetus for the BoJ to reconsider its stance. The 'quarterly pace' suggests a gradual, measured approach to avoid economic shocks, but it clearly indicates a strategic pivot away from its previous accommodative stance, a move closely watched by economists and investors worldwide.
